question: The Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) is used in children with cerebral palsy. A child classified as GMFCS Level III would MOST accurately be described as:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GMFCS Level I describes children who walk without limitations, with minor restrictions in more advanced gross motor skills such as running and jumping.

answers.text: Walks with hand-held mobility devices (crutches or walkers) indoors and outdoors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GMFCS Level III children walk using hand-held mobility devices (crutches, walkers) indoors and outdoors on level surfaces. They may use a wheeled mobility device for longer distances. They can sit independently and pull to stand.

answers.text: Self-mobility using a powered wheelchair with adaptations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GMFCS Level V describes children with minimal independent movement; even powered wheelchair use requires major adaptations. GMFCS IV children use powered wheelchairs for most distances but may walk short distances with support.

answers.text: Walks without assistive devices but with limitations outdoors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GMFCS Level II describes children who walk indoors and outdoors without assistive devices but with limitations in uneven terrain, steps, inclines, or during community distances.

overallFeedback.feedback: GMFCS Level I = walks without limitation; II = walks without aids but limitations; III = walks with hand-held aids (crutches/walkers); IV = uses wheeled mobility; V = minimal self-initiated mobility. Level III children can ambulate but require a walking aid for safety and community distances.

Correct. The GMFCS has 5 levels (I–V), with Level I being the most functional (walks without limitation) and Level V the most severe (minimal self-initiated movement). Level III specifically describes ambulatory children who need hand-held mobility aids. GMFCS is the gold standard for functional classification of CP.
